text: Southbound straight past Norwood. Train doors hiss, head lowered. Croydon board on a rainy day. Mum said learn, but I learn the estate way. Wingstop, Morley's, chips in the rain. Zigzag path from the class to the train. Concrete maze and the clock born haunted. Blue light flash, that's constant, not random. Man's got dreams of a house with a drive, but man got beef and a [trafficking humming] Back in the day, South Norwood was divided between three crews. You had the Holmesdale Boys, the HF Fanatics, the Selhurst Mandem, and the Al-Masid Brothers. Then Croydon got worse, and predators came knocking. Penge, West Norwood. Then Big Joe came along, convinced everyone that there's strength in numbers. Took three crews, made them one, and recruited a protege. Me, Liam Blake. [door banging] Then Big Joe went down. [door banging] Your generals want to know who's in charge. Have you decided? Yeah. None of them. Me? Take over? Yeah, his lawyer was sure. Why? I'm just his advisor. My thoughts exactly, bruv. Easy, bruv. Big Joe knows what he's doing. I ain't saying he doesn't. But Liam, no disrespect, bruv, you're not a leader. Sash, you're with me, right? And we-- I don't know, man. We've got to talk about this, all four of us. A crown I didn't want. Generals thinking about rebellion. I hope Big Joe is right about me. Or this all ends. JD bag and a tear in my Coke. Still hit ends like I'm proud of the post code. See ya. This is Croydon. Blaze in the cold wind. Yeah. South side living. Bare pain that I hold in. High road love, but my heart stay frozen. Still on my outside. Word is Holmesdale's looking at a proper rebellion. Good. I'll tell the others
